items.text: Fridge: 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
AESAN places the ideal refrigeration temperature between 0 and 5 °C.
Freezer: −18 °C (0 °F) or below.
A fridge thermometer helps you check both temperatures.
Use-by date: how long the food can be eaten safely. No food should be eaten once it has passed.
Before its use-by date, food can be frozen at home to make it last longer.
Best-before date: how long the food keeps its expected quality. After that date it is still safe, although it may lose flavour and texture.
After opening: follow the label's instructions for once the package is open.
Freezing date: at −18 °C food stays safe indefinitely. Freezer times tell you how long it keeps its quality.

In this app, the reminder date is the one you set, or accept with a guidance chip, when you open, freeze or thaw something, or store leftovers. If the printed use-by date comes first, the printed date wins.
Thaw in the fridge, making sure juices from meat and poultry don't drip onto other food.
In a hurry, in cold water: in a leak-proof bag, changing the water every 30 minutes, and cooking it right away.
In the microwave: cook meat and poultry right after thawing them.
Refreezing: meat and poultry thawed in the fridge can be refrozen before or after cooking. If they were thawed another way, cook them first.
AESAN does not allow food businesses to refreeze food unless it has been processed, for example cooked.
After a power cut, only refreeze food that has not fully thawed and has stayed at 5 °C or below. If you don't know how long it has been thawed, throw it away.
To freeze meat or poultry for more than 2 months in its original package, also wrap it in heavy-duty foil, plastic wrap or freezer paper, or put it in a bag.
Keep raw meat and poultry well wrapped, so their juices don't get onto other food.
Keep raw meat, poultry and fish, and their juices, away from other food. After cutting them, wash hands, cutting board, knife and worktop with hot, soapy water.
Refrigerate perishable food within 2 hours, or 1 hour if it is above 32 °C (90 °F).
Leftovers: store them in shallow containers and put them in the fridge or freezer right away. Eat them within 4 days and reheat them to 74 °C (165 °F).
Opened cans: leftovers can be kept in the can in the fridge, but they keep better in a glass or plastic container.
